turn_history.text: I have: The angles highlighted on this rectangle with different length sides can never be... ![A rectangle with the diagonals drawn in. I got acute because I assumed all the angles in the figure are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The properties of a rectangle include having all angles equal to 90 degrees. In a rectangle, opposite sides are equal in length and parallel. Remember to consider these properties when identifying angles in a rectangle.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so all the corner angles of the rectangle are 90 degrees - I get that bit now. But I'm still confused about those highlighted angles in the middle where the diagonals cross... are those the ones we're looking at, or are we talking about the corners? Because those angles in the middle don't look like they'd all be the same size to me.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: In a rectangle, the diagonals intersect at right angles, forming four congruent right triangles. The angles at the intersection of the diagonals are all right angles, each measuring 90 degrees. Remember, in a rectangle, all angles are 90 degrees.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher provides mathematically incorrect information (diagonals of a rectangle do not intersect at right angles unless it's a square), simply tells answers without engaging the student's reasoning about the central angles, and the student shows no improvement in understanding by the end.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher states explicit rules about rectangle properties, they provide incorrect information (diagonals of rectangles do not generally intersect at right angles) and fail to give direct corrective feedback on the student's specific procedural error in analyzing the central angles formed by the diagonals.
